Fig. 10. Top row Ni–Al, bottom row Ag–Cu. Leftmost is the EAM (same as Fig. 4 and Fig. 5), the three columns on the right are the MLIPs (solid-phase TI, liquid-phase calphy TI, classical level, 0 GPa). out/mlip_compare_nial_agcu/panels_ti_full.png; the individual diagrams are in out/<name>_ti/. The narrow B2+B2 band (x 0.48–0.50) and the full-width fcc+fcc band of Ag–Cu at 750–790 K are fit noise. The gap at 1100–1300 K in GRACE-FS Ni–Al and the liquid+liquid in Ag–Cu are artefacts.
Note on reading the figure (2026-11-10, answer to a user question): the white areas in Ni–Al GRACE-FS-OAM at x ≈ 0.3–0.45 for 1190–1290 K and 1040–1090 K are not single-phase regions but temperatures with no data. The calphy sweep of the liquid stops at a composition-dependent lower limit T_stop(x) (x_Ni 0.30 down to 1100 K, 0.40 to 1300 K, 0.50 to 1500 K), so at those temperatures the liquid-side end point of B2+liquid coincides with the edge of the sampled liquid range and the assembly (liquid_partial) drops those intervals as unreliable (26 intervals). The band resumes at 1300 K where the x 0.40 liquid enters. In Ag–Cu GRACE-FS-OAM, the thin fcc+liquid band at 1150 K and the liquid+liquid at 1110–1400 K (green, same phase = fit noise) are a seam in the solid-phase data: the solid TI of pure Ag only reaches 1150 K (sweep cap), x_Cu 0.9375 reaches 1145 K and 0.875 only 1101 K, so the set of points that builds the fcc G(x) changes at 1150 K and the common tangent jumps to a different solution for a single grid point. The liquid G(x) being convex upward in the middle (fit of 7 compositions) is the cause of the liquid+liquid; neither is a phase boundary.
11-10: replaced by the version from 100 K (out/mlip_compare_nial_agcu/panels_ti_full_lowT.png, panels_nial_agcu_full.py). Below the dotted line the solids alone were re-assembled from the QHA cells of each run with the same fits and sublattice models (assemble_solids_lowT.py; Ni–Al 100–890 K, Ag–Cu 100–670 K; the 670–750 K band of Ag–Cu is the gap between the QHA upper limit and the lower edge of the TI grid). In Ag–Cu the fcc+fcc two-phase field (miscibility gap) spans x ≈ 0–1 at 300 K. In Ni–Al, NiAl₃+fcc(Al) disappears at 480–580 K because the MLIP fcc(Al) solid solution (32-atom random cells + ideal mixing) becomes more stable than NiAl₃ (experimentally NiAl₃ is stable up to 1127 K). The EAM Ni–Al run has no low-temperature QHA data.
